expectation: A rich spatial folded multi-domain protein with a pocket and coherent approaching/docking/rejected objects; honest schematic semantics without invented atomistic certainty.

request.title: Why an enzyme accepts one substrate
request.topic: Explain enzyme substrate specificity to a first-year biology student using a large folded multi-domain enzyme with a binding pocket. Keep the enzyme recognizable as one connected folded structure while a compatible substrate approaches, docks into the pocket, and a differently shaped substrate approaches and is rejected. Make the pocket, the surrounding fold, and the spatial fit easy to inspect; show enough surrounding structure that the pocket belongs to a larger protein. Clearly treat this as an explanatory schematic of shape compatibility, not a deposited structure, docking calculation, or prediction that shape alone determines all binding chemistry. Create exactly one continuous, coherent scene for a 35–45 second visual lesson with concise connected subtitle narration, roughly 75–95 words. Keep the main explanatory objects visible and use a useful interactive control only if it supports the explanation. No title card, unrelated recap, or decorative motion. Choose the visual representation best suited to the explanation.
